profile.description: A profile Handle, such as ``profile_7f3a9c2e``: the one the imputer was routed on. Its sentinels and semantic types decide which cells were filled and which columns can be tested.

imputed.description: A frame Handle ``impute`` made, such as ``frame_5b6c7d8e``.

seed.description: Seed of the subsampling, the carve and the classifier. Null means a fixed default, so the same call gives the same result. Constraints: at least 0; at most 4294967295.

anyOf.description: Every ``evaluate_imputation`` dial. Null keeps every default.

min_filled_cells.description: The size floor: a column whose smaller pile, observed or filled rows, is under it is ``below_sample_floor`` and not tested. Null means 30. Constraints: at least 2.

min_samples_leaf.description: Fewest rows in a leaf of the classifier. Larger is smoother and harder to fool by memorising rows; too large and it predicts one pile for every row, which is ``uninformative``. Null means 5. Constraints: at least 1.

low_power_below.description: A tested column whose smaller pile is under this many rows is annotated ``low_power``: a pass there means not enough data to tell. Null means 250. Constraints: at least 0.

imbalance_warn_ratio.description: A tested column whose smaller pile over its larger one is under this ratio is annotated ``imbalanced_piles``. Null means 0.5. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

fdr_alpha.description: The false discovery rate across the tested columns: a column whose Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value is at or below it is ``flagged``. Raise it to flag more. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at most 1; greater than 0.

thresholds.description: The size floor, the classifier's leaf size, the annotation bands and the false discovery rate, each with its default and range. Null keeps every default.

output.description: The C2ST report Handle, the outcome census and each column's outcome. ``result.get(name)`` finds one column.

warnings.description: Caveats on this result, most actionable first. Empty when there are none.

fields.description: Always exactly `code`, `message`, `columns`, `param`, `hint`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: A caveat on a successful result: it worked, but read this first. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `code`: The warning's Error Code. Branch on this, not on ``message``.
Position 1, `message`: What happened and what to do, in one or two sentences.
Position 2, `columns`: Columns the warning concerns, or null.
Position 3, `param`: The argument the warning concerns, or null.
Position 4, `hint`: Library-written advice, or null.

omitted.description: One entry per list that was cut, naming the Operation that returns the rest. Empty when nothing was cut.

fields.description: Always exactly `field`, `shown`, `total`, `operation`, `reason`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: Something left out of a result: a capped list was cut, or a Literal Field withheld. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `field`: Name of the list field that was cut, or the path of the Literal Field withheld, such as ``top_values[].value``.
Position 1, `shown`: How many items the list holds; 0 for a withheld Literal Field.
Position 2, `total`: How many items exist; for a withheld Literal Field, how many values at that path are null.
Position 3, `operation`: The Operation that returns the rest, or null when no Operation does.
Position 4, `reason`: ``cap`` when a list was cut to its cap; ``literal_policy`` when the Operator's Literal Policy is ``deny``.

c2st.description: The new C2ST report Handle, such as ``c2st_7f3a9c2e``. It holds every column's per-frame results and the provenance.

source_frame.description: The frame Handle ``imputed`` was filled from: the observed values it is scored against.

seed.description: The seed used: yours, or the fixed default when you passed null.

census.description: Columns per outcome and verdict, over every evaluated column. Read it first.

fields.description: Always exactly `outcome`, `verdict`, `count`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: How many columns had one outcome and verdict. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `outcome`: The outcome.
Position 1, `verdict`: The verdict.
Position 2, `count`: Number of columns with both.

columns.description: Every evaluated column: ``flagged`` ones first, then dataset order. Excluded and ``dropped`` columns are not evaluated. At most 100; past 100, ``omitted`` counts the rest and names ``describe_c2st_columns``.

fields.description: Always exactly `column`, `outcome`, `verdict`, `mean_frame_z`, `p_adjusted`, `annotations`, `n_observed`, `n_filled`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: One column's C2ST outcome and score. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `column`: Column name.

Position 1, `outcome`: What happened: ``tested``, or why the test could not run. ``no_filled_cells``: nothing was missing. ``no_observed_cells``: nothing was observed. ``unfilled``: the imputed frame is still missing where the source was, as for an ``mnar``, ``passthrough`` or Drop Candidate column. ``type_not_testable``: a text or identifier column. ``below_sample_floor``: too few rows in the smaller pile. ``uninformative``: the classifier predicted one pile for every row.

Position 2, `verdict`: ``flagged`` when the filled rows are told apart from the observed ones beyond the false discovery rate: go look at this column. ``not_flagged`` when tested and not flagged. ``no_verdict`` when not tested.

Position 3, `mean_frame_z`: The score: how well a classifier tells the column's filled rows from its observed rows, as a ``z``. Near 0 means it could not; about 2 or more means it could. Null unless ``tested``.
Position 4, `p_adjusted`: The Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted one-sided p-value of ``mean_frame_z`` across the tested columns. Null unless ``tested``.

Position 5, `annotations`: Facts qualifying a tested column's score, which they never suppress: ``low_power``, ``imbalanced_piles``, ``degenerate`` (some repeats predicted one pile) and ``unseen_category`` (a filled row holds a category no observed row does). Empty when not tested.
Position 6, `n_observed`: Rows where the column was observed in the source frame.
Position 7, `n_filled`: Rows where the column was missing in the source frame, sentinels included: the rows the imputation filled.

outcome_dials.description: One entry per threshold-decided outcome, verdict or annotation any evaluated column has, with the dials that decide it.

fields.description: Always exactly `outcome`, `dials`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: The dials that decide one outcome, verdict or annotation. Turn one to change which columns get it. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `outcome`: The outcome, verdict or annotation, as in ``columns``.
Position 1, `dials`: Every dial its rule reads, with its resolved value.

fields.description: Always exactly `operation`, `dial`, `value`, `source`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: The dial whose value decided a threshold outcome. Turn it to change the outcome. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `operation`: The Operation that takes the dial.
Position 1, `dial`: The dial's argument path, such as ``thresholds.missingness.high_null_ratio``.
Position 2, `value`: The dial's resolved value.
Position 3, `source`: ``default`` when the library default decided, ``argument`` when the caller set it.
